current.title: The Great Leveler
current.author: Walter Scheidel
current.review: Bleak but rigorous — the case that only catastrophe reliably flattens inequality. Good companion reading to the policy side of things right now.

shelf.title: Sapiens
shelf.author: Yuval Noah Harari
shelf.review: Big-picture and a little too tidy in places, but the shared-fictions framing is genuinely useful for thinking about institutions.

shelf.title: The Art of War
shelf.author: Sun Tzu
shelf.review: Reread this for a strategy seminar — still holds up as a compact text on decision-making under uncertainty.

shelf.title: Antigone
shelf.author: Sophocles
shelf.review: Working on a scene study from this — the law-vs-conscience tension never gets old to perform.

shelf.title: Poor Economics
shelf.author: Banerjee & Duflo
shelf.review: The RCT-driven approach to development econ. Dense, but worth it if you're into the labor research side of things.

shelf.title: The Emperor's New Mind
shelf.author: Roger Penrose
shelf.review: Slow going outside my depth in places, but the argument about computation and consciousness stuck with me.

shelf.title: Six Characters in Search of an Author
shelf.author: Luigi Pirandello
shelf.review: A formal trick that actually earns its keep — useful to think about when writing anything metatheatrical.
